source.title: Flatness Preserves Instruction Following in Vision-Language-Action Models

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: Applies SAM during VLA fine-tuning and reports effects on counterfactual instruction-following benchmarks and real-world tasks, extending flatness/generalization work to vision-language-action models.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own SAM interventions and measurements relevant to generalization and flatness. Cited findings from prior work and hyperparameter sweeps used only to select settings are not extracted as rows. The study evaluates counterfactual/OOD instruction following, which is distinct from same-distribution test error; V1–V8 therefore are not directly tested.
record.test_reason: The study applies flatness-preserving optimization to improve VLA instruction following. Its sharpness measurements and counterfactual task success do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness ranking of training–test gaps. It reports none of the comparisons required by V1–V6 or V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: SAM improves counterfactual instruction following on the reported benchmarks and real-world tasks, global application beats selective application, and guidance can provide further gains. Complementarity is benchmark-dependent. Absolute success remains low, and SAM approximately doubles training compute. The geometry comparisons support an association rather than establishing that flatness causes the improvement.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAM while fine-tuning pretrained VLAs on robot data and measures counterfactual instruction following, representation probes, and action-head landscape geometry; it does not reproduce the listed natural-label generalization or memorization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance differs by SAM scope (global versus individual components), benchmark, model architecture, SAM neighborhood radius, and combination with inference-time guidance. Selective component application does not improve over the standard VLA; guidance matches LangGap average and is lower on LIBERO-CF.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM improves reported counterfactual instruction-following success for both VLA architectures and in real-world evaluation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM fine-tuning can improve counterfactual instruction following on limited robot data; the OpenVLA-OFT LIBERO-CF baseline requires clarification.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM-finetuned π0.5 has lower measured action-head sharpness and maximum Hessian eigenvalue alongside higher counterfactual success.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lower action-head sharpness and curvature accompany improved counterfactual instruction following in the reported standard-versus-SAM comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Selective SAM yields 23.0%, 22.7%, and 21.0% success, below standard fine-tuning's 26.6% and global SAM's 42.6%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Global SAM outperforms individual-component SAM on the reported LIBERO-PRO Task evaluation.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding guidance raises average success on LIBERO-PRO Task, leaves LangGap unchanged, and lowers LIBERO-CF success.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of adding inference-time guidance to SAM depends on the benchmark.

record.problems: The paper explicitly notes that absolute success rates remain low. Sharpness and Hessian calculations are restricted to the action head because of compute and memory constraints. Reported success rates do not include uncertainty estimates. Real-world evaluation uses five task layouts and the text gives differing rollout counts in its description (five rollouts for three counterfactual tasks, then ten rollouts per counterfactual task).
record.rows_left_out: No relevant separately reported result rows omitted. Hyperparameter sweeps for selecting SAM ρ and CFG guidance scale are not included because the text says they were used to find the best setting; benchmark outcome rows for the selected settings and the explicit component ablation are retained.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local-connectivity effects.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epochs and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout's effect on classifier held-out error. Language-input dropout for guidance is not this comparison.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus training–test gaps at similarly low training loss, including ranking against norm and margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected examples.

record.verdict_notes: The exclusion rests on the specific comparisons and measures in V1–V8, not on a blanket exclusion of OOD generalization. No listed-version verdict is warranted, and no omitted result bearing on those versions was found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not compare fitting random labels with generalization on natural labels.
No network-width sweep past an interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison; AdamW is the base optimizer.
No batch-size comparison of generalization gaps.

The paper measures sharpness and a Hessian eigenvalue, but does not test magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness against generalization gaps among networks of one convolutional family at similarly low training loss.
